    Is McNeese State a historically black college?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    No, McNeese State University is not a Historically Black College or University (HBCU). Located in Lake Charles, Louisiana, it is a public university within the University of Louisiana System. While it serves a diverse student body, it does not hold the official federal designation as an HBCU. 
    Key Details About McNeese State University: 
    • Established: Founded in 1939 as Lake Charles Junior College.
    • Location: Lake Charles, Louisiana.
    • Affiliation: University of Louisiana System. 
    For context, Louisiana does have several prominent HBCUs, such as Southern University, Grambling State University, Xavier University of Louisiana, and Dillard University, but McNeese is not among them.

      Description

      McNeese State University is a public university in Lake Charles, Louisiana, United States. Founded in 1939 as Lake Charles Junior College, it was renamed McNeese Junior College after John McNeese, an early local educator. The present name was adopted in 1970. Wikipedia
      Address: 4205 Ryan St, Lake Charles, LA 70605
      Mascot: Rowdy
      President: Wade Rousse
      Students: 6,556 (fall 2025)
      Campus: Urban, 121 acres (49 ha)
      Undergraduate tuition and fees: In-state tuition 8,460 USD, Out-of-state tuition 9,960 USD (2023 – 24) IPEDS
      Acceptance rate: 78.3% (2024) IPEDS
      Nicknames: Cowboys, Cowgirls
      Colors: Royal blue, Sunflower gold
      Established: September 1939; 86 years ago
      Motto: Excellence With A Personal Touch
      Phone: (800) 622-3352
      Hours:
